At the END of year t, effective 31 December 2018, the 2016 and prior years closed (RITC) into Syndicate 1955 for 42.5m, with a quota share back to the 2017 year (p9, p50). Earlier, in 2014, 6118 took 11.54% of 1955's back-year reserves (2008-2013 years) (1955's 2015 report p5; 6118's 2016 report p6: 'An adjustment of 46.5m was made to premium written during 2014 in respect of the 2008 to 2013 Years of Account, bringing total premium written during 2014 to 71.5m. This amount represented an 11.547% share of Barbican Syndicate 1955's written premium for the 2008 to 2013 Years of Account').
6118_2018.overlapping_history: YES. The 2014 column is not the same object in consecutive reports. 6118's 2016 table (p38, page image) prints 2014 at 120,357 / 125,156 / 131,412; the 2017 table (p36, page image) 121,093 / 119,653 / 125,747 / 101,239 (end-2017); the 2018 table's end-2017 cell for 2014 is 21,267 (p39). The 2014 end-2017 cell therefore falls 101,239 -> 21,267 (-79%) between the 2017 and 2018 reports, about 80m of ultimate claims, with no restatement note (grep of the 2018 report for restat/reclass/2008/back year finds only the ADC paragraph). The 2017 column carried the 2008-2013 back-year cession (premium adjustment 46.5m inside 2014's 71.5m); the 2018 column carries the pure 2014 year. The 2015-2017 cells are also restated by +3 to +4% (2015 41,766 -> 43,126; 2016 84,968 -> 88,101; 2017 142,866 -> 149,075) although 6118 reports in sterling, so FX does not explain it. The back-year's own 2018 development is in neither the M cells nor identifiable.

For all other years of account, amounts ceded from Barbican Syndicate 1955 to the Syndicate are taken net of external reinsurance.' 1955's 2015 report p5: cessions to 6118 'have been calculated on the Syndicate's result net of external reinsurance'. p6 of 2018 says the 2017 year was 'gross of external reinsurance and net of acquisition costs' (inconsistent with p20). So the table headed 'Gross' mixes a gross-of-external-RI 2018 (and 2017) cohort with u<=2016 cohorts that are net of 1955's external reinsurance, plus the 6118 retrocession (reinsurers' share 93,717 against gross 211,626, p18).
